title: MiG-21bis (DCS)
intro: The MiG-21bis is a small, fast Soviet jet fighter from the 1970s, built to shoot down bombers. The cockpit is cramped, with switches spread over both side walls. The manual splits it into segments: right vertical and horizontal (RV, RH), centre (C), left vertical and horizontal (LV, LH) and the stick (PS). The radar screen sits under the gunsight, and the twist grip on the throttle moves the radar gate and the sight ring.

areas.name: Above the gunsight
areas.text: Above the gunsight sits the control box for the jamming container, and, if fitted, the boxes for the gun containers and the special bomb.

panels.name: SPS-141-100 jamming container control box
panels.text: This small box sits above the gunsight. It runs the SPS-141-100, a pod under the belly that sends out jamming signals against enemy radars and throws out chaff and flares.
panels.context: The box only appears when the pod is hung under the plane. After the main switch is on, the pod needs about 30 seconds to warm up before its ready light comes on.

controls.name: ON / OFF switch (SPS main power)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The pod is powered and starts to warm up.

controls.text: This switch turns the jamming pod on or off. It is the first switch to use on this box.
controls.context: After switching on, the pod needs about 30 seconds to warm up. A light on the box shows when the pod is ready.

controls.name: Transmit / Receive switch

positions.name: TRANSMIT
positions.text: The pod sends out jamming signals.

controls.text: This switch decides whether the pod only listens for enemy radars or also sends out its own jamming signal.
controls.context: The pilot keeps it on receive while only watching for threats and uses transmit when active jamming is wanted.

controls.name: Program I / II switch

positions.name: I
positions.text: The first jamming pattern is used.

positions.name: II
positions.text: The second jamming pattern is used.

controls.text: This switch picks one of two stored jamming patterns, called I and II.
controls.context: Each pattern is a different way of confusing the enemy radar. The pilot picks the one that fits the threat.

controls.name: Continuous / Impulse switch

positions.name: CONTINUOUS
positions.text: The jamming signal is sent without a break.

positions.name: IMPULSE
positions.text: The jamming signal is sent in short bursts.

controls.text: This switch chooses how the jamming signal is sent: all the time (continuous) or in short bursts (impulse).
controls.context: It works together with the pattern switch and sets the rhythm of the jamming.

controls.name: Test button
controls.text: This button starts a self-test of the jamming pod. It checks that the pod works.
controls.context: The manual says the test can be run after the pod has warmed up.

controls.name: Dispenser Auto / Manual switch

positions.name: AUTO
positions.text: The dispenser launches its decoys by itself.

positions.name: MANUAL
positions.text: The dispenser launches only when the pilot presses the launch button.

controls.text: This switch tells the pod's chaff and flare dispenser to throw out its decoys by itself (auto) or only when the pilot presses the button (manual).
controls.context: Chaff is a cloud of metal strips that fools radar missiles. Flares are hot burning decoys that fool heat-seeking missiles.

controls.name: Flare program switch (Off / Parallel / Full)

positions.name: PARALLEL
positions.text: A program that launches flares in a regular pattern; the manual describes a program that launches them in pairs.

positions.name: FULL
positions.text: The second launching program; the manual describes a fast single-flare program.

controls.text: This switch picks the flare launching program. The middle and the top position launch flares in different patterns, and the bottom position is off.
controls.context: The game names the positions Off, Parallel and Full. The manual calls the programs in pairs and single fast; it does not say which name is which.

controls.name: Manual launch button cover
controls.text: This is the cover over the manual launch button. The pilot lifts it before pressing the button, so the button cannot be pressed by accident.
controls.context: It protects the button for throwing out chaff and flares by hand.

controls.name: Manual chaff / flare launch button
controls.text: Pressing this button throws out chaff and flares by hand, when the dispenser is set to manual.
controls.context: The pilot uses it when a radar or heat-seeking missile threatens the plane.

panels.name: UPK-23-250-2 gun container control box
panels.text: This small box controls the gun containers that can hang under the wings. Each container holds a double-barrel 23 mm cannon.
panels.context: The box only appears in the cockpit when the containers are on the inner wing stations. The pilot switches the containers on and chooses which gun fires.

controls.name: UPK power switch (On / Off)
controls.text: This switch gives electric power to the gun containers under the wings.
controls.context: Without power the containers cannot fire. The manual lists it as the first of the box's two controls.

controls.name: Gun selector (main gun / UPK guns)

positions.name: MAIN GUN
positions.text: The trigger fires the cannon in the fuselage.

positions.name: UPK GUNS
positions.text: The trigger fires the guns in the wing containers.

controls.text: This switch chooses which guns the trigger fires: the gun built into the fuselage or the guns in the wing containers.
controls.context: The game names it 'Gsh / UPK'. The pilot picks the gun that fits the target before the attack.

controls.name: LOAD 1-3 buttons (UPK gun charging)
controls.text: These three buttons are named LOAD 1, 2 and 3 on the box. The game calls them 'Charge' buttons for the gun containers.
controls.context: The manual does not describe these three buttons. They look like the three loading buttons of the fuselage gun, which charge the gun with a small explosive cartridge.

panels.name: IAB control box (special bomb)
panels.text: This box appears above the gunsight when a special practice bomb for a big explosion is hung under the belly. It holds the switches for dropping that one bomb.
panels.context: DCS has no real nuclear weapons. The manual says the box belongs to a bomb that only imitates some effects of a tactical nuclear explosion.

controls.name: EMERGENCY DROP switch
controls.text: This switch is the emergency drop for the special bomb. It lets the pilot get rid of the bomb in a hurry.
controls.context: The manual lists it as the first control of the box. It only works when the next switch is set to armed.

controls.name: Emergency drop ARMED / NOT ARMED switch
controls.text: This switch makes the emergency drop active (armed) or inactive (not armed).
controls.context: The manual says it applies to the emergency drop only.

controls.name: Tactical drop switch (game: 'Tactical Jettison')
controls.text: The game names this switch 'Tactical Jettison'. It is part of the special bomb box; the manual lists a combat drop switch for the normal release of the bomb.
controls.context: The manual does not describe this switch separately from the box.

controls.name: Weapon selector (game: 'Special AB / Missile-Rocket-Bombs-Cannon')
controls.text: This selector chooses whether the special bomb or the other weapons are used. The manual says it must be up for the bomb.
controls.context: It has no effect on the plane's other weapons while it is set to the bomb.

controls.name: Switch named 'Brake Chute' in the game
controls.text: The game names this switch 'Brake Chute'. It belongs to the special bomb box.
controls.context: The manual does not describe it separately. It only says that one switch of the box, the RETARDED switch, must stay down all the time.

controls.name: Detonation GROUND / AIR switch
controls.text: This switch picks whether the bomb explodes on the ground or in the air.
controls.context: The manual says it should be left on ground only.

areas.name: Left part of the instrument panel
areas.text: On the left of the main panel are the take-off rocket controls.

panels.name: SPRD take-off rockets and ASO chaff / flare dispenser
panels.text: The SPRD are small rockets that can be hung under the plane to help the take-off. The same mounts can hold the ASO container, which throws out chaff and flares as decoys.
panels.context: The rocket power switches are on the right wall. The drop button for the rockets, which also launches the decoys, is on the throttle.

controls.name: SPRD start button cover
controls.text: This is the cover over the button that fires the take-off rockets.
controls.context: The pilot lifts it before pressing the button.

controls.name: SPRD rocket boosters start button
controls.text: This button fires the take-off rockets by hand, for about 7 seconds of extra push.
controls.context: The manual says they start by themselves at about 120 to 150 km/h on the take-off run, so firing them by hand is not recommended.

areas.name: Main instrument panel
areas.text: The main instrument panel is in front of the pilot. It has the gunsight on top, the weapon selection, the radar screen and the dials for flying and for the engine.

panels.name: ASP-PFD optical gunsight
panels.text: The ASP-PFD is the gunsight on top of the instrument panel. It projects an aiming ring (the pipper) and a fixed net of lines onto a glass plate in front of the pilot's eyes.
panels.context: The pilot sets what is being aimed (guns, rockets, bombs or missiles) and the size of the target on the sight. The sight then moves the ring to the right place and shows lights and distance scales.

controls.name: Gun / rocket-missiles switch

positions.name: GUN
positions.text: The sight is set up for the cannon.

positions.name: MISSILES-ROCKETS
positions.text: The sight is set up for rockets and missiles.

controls.text: This switch tells the sight what is being aimed: the cannon or the rockets and missiles.
controls.context: The sight draws the aiming ring differently for each weapon, so the pilot sets it before the attack.

controls.name: Firing / bombing switch

positions.name: FIRING
positions.text: Shooting mode, used for guns, rockets and missiles.

positions.name: BOMBARDMENT
positions.text: Bombing mode, used only for bombs.

controls.text: This switch tells the sight whether to aim for shooting or for dropping bombs.
controls.context: The manual says bombardment mode is used only for bombs and firing mode for all other weapons.

controls.name: Auto / manual switch

positions.name: AUTO
positions.text: The sight works out distance, target size and angle correction by itself.

positions.name: MANUAL
positions.text: The pilot enters target size and angle correction and measures the distance.

controls.text: This switch decides who sets the distance and the target size: the sight itself (auto) or the pilot (manual).
controls.context: In auto mode the sight uses radar data or preset values. In manual mode the pilot enters the target size and measures the distance by eye.

controls.name: Pipper mode lever (missile / gyro)

positions.name: MSL
positions.text: A steady aiming ring, used for missile aiming.

positions.name: GYRO
positions.text: A lively aiming ring that follows the plane's turning; the weapon hits if fired at the right distance.

controls.text: This lever chooses how the aiming ring moves. In missile mode the ring is calm. In gyro mode it reacts to the plane's turns and jumps around more.
controls.context: The manual uses missile mode for missile aiming and gyro mode for targets that do not turn hard, such as ground targets.

controls.name: Target size knob
controls.text: This knob sets how big the target is, in metres. The sight uses it to work out the distance.
controls.context: The manual says to set 10 to 12 metres for ground targets when the real size is unknown.

controls.name: Target size scale
controls.text: This small red window shows the target size that was set with the target size knob.
controls.context: It shows the size in metres for all modes except the automatic gun mode, where the scale on the knob itself is read.

controls.name: Angular (intercept angle) correction knob
controls.text: This knob sets the lead angle, which is how far ahead of the target the ring is placed.
controls.context: In automatic mode the sight turns this knob by itself for the chosen weapon. In manual mode the pilot sets it.

controls.name: Angular correction scale
controls.text: This small window shows the lead angle in degrees that is set on the sight.
controls.context: It is read together with the angular correction knob.

controls.name: Pipper On / Off switch
controls.text: This switch turns the aiming ring (pipper) on or off.
controls.context: The pilot can aim with the ring or with the fixed net of lines.

controls.name: Fixed net On / Off switch
controls.text: This switch turns the fixed net, a pattern of fixed aiming lines, on or off.
controls.context: The manual says the fixed net is used against targets that turn hard, because the ring would go outside the glass.

controls.name: Pipper light control knob
controls.text: This knob makes the aiming ring brighter or darker.
controls.context: The pilot sets it so the ring is clear against the sky or the ground.

controls.name: Fixed net light control knob
controls.text: This knob changes the brightness of the fixed net of aiming lines.
controls.context: It is set to the light of the day, together with the pipper brightness.

controls.name: Scale backlight control knob
controls.text: This knob changes the brightness of the lighting behind the scales on the sight.
controls.context: It is mostly needed when flying at night.

controls.name: Backlight preset knob
controls.text: This knob presets the backlight of the sight before the flight.
controls.context: The manual says it is not meant for the pilot to use in flight; it is set up before the flight.

controls.name: LAUNCH AUTHORISED light
controls.text: This orange light comes on when the target is inside the range of the chosen weapon.
controls.context: The manual says the pilot should use the weapon one or two seconds after this light comes on.

controls.name: RADAR LOCK-ON light
controls.text: This green light shows that the radar is locked on a target and is measuring its distance.
controls.context: It only works when the radar is used for the distance, either for air-to-air missiles or in fixed-beam mode for ground attacks.

controls.name: BREAK-OFF light
controls.text: This red light tells the pilot to stop the attack and pull away.
controls.context: The manual says the pilot should break off decisively when it lights up, for both air and ground targets. The launch light goes out at the same time.

controls.name: Distance scales and needle
controls.text: The top of the sight has four distance scales and one needle. The needle shows the distance to the target on the scale of the chosen weapon.
controls.context: The pilot has to know which scale fits the weapon: guns and rockets against ground targets, air-to-air missiles, small distances for gun attacks, and the ring size.

controls.name: Missile launch distance scale
controls.text: This small window at the top left of the sight shows the distance to a radar-locked target for air-to-air missiles.
controls.context: The manual says the pilot does not need to watch it much, because the launch lights already say when to fire.

panels.name: Weapon selection panel (upper centre)
panels.text: This group of controls chooses which weapon is ready: air or ground targets, the type of missile, and which wing station is used. It also holds the buttons that load the cannon.
panels.context: The manual puts the weapon system in four steps: switch on, select, aim and launch. This panel is the select step. The power switches for the weapons are on the right wall.

controls.name: Weapon master mode switch (Air / Ground)

positions.name: AIR
positions.text: The weapons are set for air targets.

positions.name: GROUND
positions.text: The weapons are set for ground targets.

controls.text: This switch tells the weapon system if the pilot wants to attack aircraft (air) or targets on the ground.
controls.context: The manual says infrared missiles are used with the air mode, even against hot ground targets.

controls.name: Missile type switch (IR / neutral / radar guided)

positions.name: NEUTRAL
positions.text: No air-to-air missile type is selected.

controls.text: This switch picks the kind of air-to-air missile: one that follows heat, one that follows a radar beam, or none.
controls.context: Heat-seeking missiles use the top position and radar-guided missiles the bottom one. The middle position is neutral, used for ground attacks.

controls.name: Gun load / reload buttons 1-3
controls.text: These three buttons load the fuselage cannon. Each one fires a small explosive cartridge that charges the gun.
controls.context: The first button loads the gun. If the gun jams, the next unused button is pressed to clear it, so the gun can be loaded three times in total.

controls.name: Gun ready light
controls.text: This green light shows that the cannon is loaded and ready.
controls.context: The light is off when the gun is empty, not loaded or jammed.

controls.name: Pylon and weapon type selector knob
controls.text: This big knob chooses the wing station and the weapon to be fired. Its positions are arranged around it like the numbers on a clock.
controls.context: On the manual's clock: bombs and rocket pods use the left part, S-24 rockets the top part and air-to-air missiles the right and lower part. It also sets pairs of launchers.

controls.name: SUA light (high angle of attack warning)
controls.text: This light warns the pilot that the wing is getting close to a stall. The more quickly the pilot raises the nose, the earlier it lights.
controls.context: The manual says it can come on as early as an angle of attack of 22 degrees. It is checked with the warning-light test buttons.

controls.name: Gun camera
controls.text: This is the gun camera, which films what the pilot aims at. The manual's drawing does not show it.
controls.context: It is switched on with the gun camera power switch on the right wall.

controls.name: Missile readiness lights (1, 2 and R-60)
controls.text: These three green lights show that the heat-seeking missile has locked on a target. Light 1 is for the left wing, 2 for the right wing and the third for R-60 missiles.
controls.context: The pilot needs to see the light and hear the lock tone. If one of the two is missing, the lock may only be short or on a false heat source.

panels.name: Radar scope and jamming-filter buttons
panels.text: This is the round radar screen with a row of buttons near it. The screen shows targets in front of the plane. The buttons change how the radar deals with enemy jamming and with weather.
panels.context: The radar of the MiG-21bis is called RP-22 Sapphire. It needs time to warm up. The pilot turns the radar on at the panel on the right wall.

controls.name: Radar screen
controls.text: This round screen shows what the radar sees in front of the plane. Targets appear as marks, and a locked target is shown as a bar with distance marks.
controls.context: The pilot moves a small gate over a target with the throttle twist grip and then presses the lock-on button on the stick.

controls.name: Radar polar filter knob
controls.text: The game names this knob 'Radar Polar Filter'. The manual describes a controllable sun filter on the radar screen.
controls.context: The manual does not say which knob moves the filter; the game only gives this name.

controls.name: Radar screen illumination gain
controls.text: This is the brightness of the radar screen picture. The manual says it is not meant for the pilot to use.
controls.context: It is set up on the ground and not touched in flight.

controls.name: Radar screen magnetization erase button
controls.text: This button erases the picture that stays on the radar screen.
controls.context: The game names it 'Radar Screen Magnetic Reset'. The manual only lists it in the segment drawing.

controls.name: Jamming filter: continuous button
controls.text: This button sets the radar filter to its continuous mode. It is one of several buttons for working against interference on the radar picture.
controls.context: The game names it 'Radar Interferes - Continues'. The manual only names the button in its drawing.

controls.name: Jamming filter: intermittent button
controls.text: This button sets the radar filter to its intermittent mode, meant for interference that comes and goes.
controls.context: The game names it 'Radar Interferes - Temporary'. The manual only names the button in its drawing.

controls.name: Jamming filter: passive button
controls.text: This button sets the radar filter to its passive mode, one of the settings against interference.
controls.context: The game names it 'Radar Interferes - Passive'. The manual only names the button in its drawing.

controls.name: Jamming filter: weather button
controls.text: This button sets the radar filter to its weather mode, meant for interference caused by the weather.
controls.context: The game names it 'Radar Interferes - Weather'. The manual only names the button in its drawing.

controls.name: Interrogation (IFF) button
controls.text: This button asks the targets on the radar screen: friend or foe? Friendly aircraft are then drawn as a double line for a few seconds.
controls.context: The manual says friendly targets go back to looking like enemies after a few seconds, so the pilot must stay careful.

controls.name: Low-speed target (LST) button
controls.text: This button makes the radar better at picking up slow targets, such as slow aircraft, helicopters and drones.
controls.context: It is pressed in search mode. The cancel button brings the radar back to normal.

controls.name: Radar self-test button
controls.text: This button tests the radar after it has warmed up. False targets appear on the screen for the test.
controls.context: The manual lets the pilot lock a false target during the test to see all the control lights come on in sequence.

controls.name: Radar reset / cancel button
controls.text: This button cancels a target lock and sends the radar back to search. It also leaves the low-speed mode.
controls.context: The manual calls it CANCEL or RESET. It is also used if the self-test does not start.

controls.name: Radar emission cover
controls.text: This is the cover over the switch that picks the kind of radar emission. The pilot lifts it before using the switch.
controls.context: The game names it 'Radar emission - Cover'.

controls.name: Radar emission switch (Combat / Training)

positions.name: LIVE
positions.text: The live combat signal is used.

controls.text: This switch picks a training or a live signal for the radar-guided missile. The cockpit list calls it the SAR missile radar frequency selector.
controls.context: The game names it 'Radar emission - Combat/Training'. The manual lists the switch but does not explain the two positions further.

panels.name: Flight and navigation instruments
panels.text: These round dials tell the pilot how fast the plane flies, how high, whether it is level and where it is heading. They sit in the middle of the main panel.
panels.context: The manual says the pilot learns which dials matter in each phase of flight. Several of them need the main Pitot tube (the air tube outside) to work, with the spare Pitot tube as a backup.

controls.name: IAS indicator (airspeed)
controls.text: This dial shows the speed of the plane through the air in kilometres per hour, up to 1600. A small window shows a 1 when the speed is over 1000.
controls.context: The dial works as long as the main Pitot tube works. If the tube freezes, the pilot switches to the spare Pitot tube with the lever.

controls.name: Barometric altimeter and pressure knob
controls.text: This dial shows the height above sea level in the air pressure scale. The small needle shows kilometres and the big needle tens of metres. The knob sets the local air pressure.
controls.context: The pilot sets the pressure in the small window with the button, so the height reads correctly. It works with the main Pitot installation.

controls.name: KPP attitude indicator
controls.text: This dial, the KPP, shows whether the plane is level. It shows bank, nose up or down, and sideways slip. It also holds needles for the landing radio beams.
controls.context: It is the artificial horizon for flying by instruments. Other systems such as the autopilot use its data, so a gyro that has drifted should be reset.

controls.name: KPP gyro reset button
controls.text: This button resets the gyro of the KPP, the spinning wheel that keeps the horizon steady. The game names it 'KPP Cage'.
controls.context: The plane must fly straight and level while the reset runs. It takes 3 to 4 seconds and a light shows it.

controls.name: KPP horizon set knob
controls.text: This knob moves the pitch setting of the KPP. The game names it 'KPP Set'.
controls.context: The manual says the knob next to the reset button serves to change the pitch setting if needed.

controls.name: NPP course system (compass)
controls.text: This dial, the NPP, is the plane's compass. It shows the heading, the direction to a radio station and a course to follow. Needles show landing radio beams.
controls.context: Before taxiing the pilot lets it line up with the Earth's magnetic field using a button. The NPP needle points to 45 degrees right when no radio signal is received.

controls.name: NPP course set knob
controls.text: This knob sets the course the pilot wants to fly, for example the runway direction.
controls.context: The pointer at the head of the NPP moves to the set course. The pilot then flies so that it lines up.

controls.name: NPP course magnetic correction button
controls.text: Holding this button lets the compass card turn until it fits the magnetic field of the Earth. Release it when the card stops.
controls.context: The manual says this normally needs to be done once before taxiing, and again on the runway if the course reading is wrong.

controls.name: DA-200 vertical speed, turn and slip indicator
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the plane climbs or sinks (the variometer). It also has a ball for sideslip and a needle for the rate of turn.
controls.context: It can replace the KPP for flying a safe landing pattern if the KPP fails. It needs the gyros switched on for the turn needle.

controls.name: Variometer set knob
controls.text: The game names this knob 'Variometer Set'. It adjusts the climb-and-sink dial.
controls.context: The manual does not describe this knob further.

controls.name: M and TAS indicator (Mach and true airspeed)
controls.text: This dial shows the speed as a Mach number with its thick needle, and the true speed with the thin needle.
controls.context: Mach 1 is the speed of sound. The dial works as long as the main Pitot tube works.

controls.name: Radio altimeter
controls.text: This dial shows the height above the ground, up to 600 metres, measured straight below the plane.
controls.context: The pilot reads it quickly when landing or flying low. It works when the radio altimeter power switch is on.

controls.name: Radio altimeter low altitude selector knob
controls.text: This knob sets the height at which the low altitude warning light comes on, or switches the warning off. The game lists heights from 100 to 400 metres.
controls.context: When the matching mode is on, the autopilot can pull the plane out of a low altitude zone.

controls.name: Low altitude warning light
controls.text: This light comes on when the plane flies lower than the height that was set on the radio altimeter.
controls.context: It warns the pilot to climb or check the height.

controls.name: Accelerometer (G meter)
controls.text: This dial shows how hard the plane pulls in turns. It shows the load now and the highest and lowest loads reached.
controls.context: The pilot watches it when carrying weapons, so the load limit is not exceeded and the stores do not fall off.

controls.name: Accelerometer reset button
controls.text: This button sets the highest and lowest recorded loads back to normal.
controls.context: The pilot presses it to start a new count.

controls.name: UUA-1 angle-of-attack gauge
controls.text: This dial shows the angle of attack: how steeply the wing meets the air. The yellow-black sector is the best area and the red-black sector is dangerous.
controls.context: The manual says the plane stalls at 33 degrees and can be flown safely up to 28 degrees.

controls.name: ARU-3VM gauge
controls.text: This dial shows the setting of the ARU, which controls how strongly the tail reacts to the stick. It has a speed scale and an altitude scale.
controls.context: At low speed the needle should be at the left end (long arm). The manual says the needle must be there before landing and above 7000 metres.

controls.name: Nosecone position indicator and manual control
controls.text: This dial shows how far the cone at the air intake is pushed out. The knob moves the black-and-white needle to set the cone by hand.
controls.context: The cone is normally automatic. If it fails, the pilot switches to manual and sets it using the table in the manual.

controls.name: RSBN distance indicator
controls.text: This counter shows the distance to the selected RSBN ground station, a short-range navigation beacon.
controls.context: It always points to the RSBN station if the receiver is on and the signal is received.

controls.name: Gyro reset indication light
controls.text: This light comes on while the gyros of the autopilot, compass and radar are being reset.
controls.context: After a reset it goes off after 2 to 3 seconds.

controls.name: Clock, stopwatch and flight timer
controls.text: This is the plane's mechanical clock with a stopwatch and a flight-time counter. The two levers wind it and start and stop it.
controls.context: The game names them 'Mech clock left lever' and 'Mech clock right lever'. The manual only lists the clock in the drawing.

controls.name: Pitot tube selector lever (main / auxiliary)

positions.name: MAIN
positions.text: The main Pitot tube is used.

positions.name: AUXILIARY
positions.text: The auxiliary Pitot tube is used.

controls.text: This lever chooses which of two air tubes outside the plane feeds the speed and height dials: the main one or the auxiliary one.
controls.context: If the main tube freezes or fails, the pilot switches to the auxiliary tube.

controls.name: Main Pitot tube, mirror and AoA sensor heater switch
controls.text: This switch heats the main air tube, the mirror and the angle-of-attack sensor so they do not freeze.
controls.context: The manual says to switch the Pitot heating on whenever the outside temperature is around 0 degrees Celsius or lower.

controls.name: Auxiliary Pitot tube heater switch
controls.text: This switch heats the auxiliary air tube.
controls.context: It is switched on together with the main heating in cold air. The game also names it 'Emergency Pitot Tube Heating'.

panels.name: Engine and systems gauges
panels.text: These dials show how the engine and the systems are doing: engine speed, exhaust heat, fuel, oil and the pressures of the hydraulic and air systems.
panels.context: The pilot glances at them during start-up, take-off and every few minutes in flight. They are on the right half of the main panel.

controls.name: Engine RPM gauge (tachometer)
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the engine turns, as a percentage of the highest allowed speed. Two needles show the two compressor stages.
controls.context: The manual always means the first needle when it speaks of a percentage. The first needle should never exceed 103.5 percent.

controls.name: Engine exhaust temperature gauge
controls.text: This dial shows the temperature of the exhaust gas behind the engine, in degrees Celsius.
controls.context: The manual says it must never exceed 850 degrees. The pilot waits for 600 degrees on the runway before lighting the afterburner.

controls.name: Oil pressure gauge
controls.text: This dial shows the pressure of the engine oil. Normal pressure is 3 to 4 units.
controls.context: The low oil pressure light next to it comes on if the pressure drops below 1 unit or metal bits are found in the oil.

controls.name: Low oil pressure light
controls.text: This light comes on if the engine oil pressure is too low or metal particles are found in the oil.
controls.context: The manual says to abort the mission and land if it comes on.

controls.name: Fuel quantity gauge and setting knob
controls.text: This dial shows how many litres of fuel are left. The knob sets the starting amount before the flight.
controls.context: If fuel from some tanks is not used, the dial reads too much, so the pilot also watches the fuel lights.

controls.name: Hydraulic pressure gauges
controls.text: These two dials show the pressure in the two hydraulic systems, the main one and the command one. Hydraulics move heavy parts with oil under high pressure.
controls.context: If the pressure falls low, a warning light comes on. The manual says to land if there are hydraulic problems.

controls.name: Voltmeter
controls.text: This dial shows the voltage of the direct-current electric system.
controls.context: The battery should show about 22.5 to 24.5 volts and the generator 28.5 volts. A slowly falling voltage means the generator failed.

controls.name: Battery capacity meter
controls.text: This dial shows how much charge the battery has.
controls.context: The manual lists it only in the drawing of the central segment.

controls.name: Wheel brake air pressure gauges
controls.text: These two needles show the air pressure for the left and right wheel brakes. The brakes work with compressed air.
controls.context: The manual says the pressure should be at least 8 before taxiing, and normally 10.

controls.name: Cockpit altitude and pressure gauge
controls.text: This dial shows the air pressure inside the cockpit.
controls.context: It sits in the central segment next to the other pressure gauges.

panels.name: Warning light groups and test buttons
panels.text: The plane has many warning lights, grouped in tables. The more important a table is, the higher it sits. Red means warning, orange means watch it, and green means a normal message.
panels.context: Before engine start the pilot presses a test button to check that all the lights work. Every table has a knob to test it and to set its brightness.

controls.name: Check warning lights / day-night buttons
match: label:Check Warning Lights - Set Warning Light Day/Night
controls.text: These buttons check the warning lights. While one is held, all the lights of its table are on. Turning the matching knob changes the brightness.
controls.context: The manual says to press any of them before start to check that all warning lights work, including the SUA light and the three green sight lights.

controls.name: Warning lights group test and backlight knobs
controls.text: These six knobs test one group of warning lights each and set how bright the group is. The groups are control systems, rocket pods, weapons, fuel, engine and main systems, and gear, flaps and air brakes.
controls.context: They sit at the tables of lights around the cockpit. The game offers the test as the group of day-night buttons above.

controls.name: SORC main warning light and button
controls.text: This is the main warning light of the plane (SORC). It lights when the system sees a problem. Pressing it acknowledges the warning.
controls.context: The manual lists it in the drawing; at start-up it is on together with the other red lights.

controls.name: Tactical release 'bombs armed' warning light
controls.text: This light comes on when the bombs have been armed with the tactical release switch.
controls.context: It reminds the pilot that bombs will explode on impact.

panels.name: Emergency handles and jettison buttons (front panel)
panels.text: On the front panel are handles and buttons the pilot rarely uses: emergency brakes, the nose wheel brake, the emergency gear release and the buttons that drop the weapons or fuel tanks.
panels.context: They are for special situations. The covers over the jettison buttons are lifted before use so nothing is dropped by accident.

controls.name: Emergency brakes lever
controls.text: This lever switches on emergency braking of the wheels, for when the normal brakes do not work.
controls.context: The game names it 'Emergency Brake' and gives it an on and off toggle. The manual only lists it in the drawing.

controls.name: Nose gear brake lever
controls.text: This lever turns the nose wheel brake on or off. When horizontal, the brake is on.
controls.context: The pilot switches it on before the engine run-up on the runway and off again after landing when taxiing speed is reached.

controls.name: Emergency nose gear release handle
controls.text: Pulling this handle lowers the nose wheel by the emergency system, if the normal system does not work.
controls.context: The game names it 'Nose Gear Emergency Release Handle'. There is a second emergency handle for the main wheels, on the right wall.

controls.name: Outer pylons jettison cover (pylons 3-4)
controls.text: This cover protects the button for dropping everything from the outer wing stations.
controls.context: The pilot lifts the cover first and then presses the button underneath.

controls.name: Outer pylons emergency jettison button
controls.text: This button drops all the weapons and tanks from the outer wing stations (3 and 4) at once.
controls.context: It is for emergencies. The button is under a red cap.

controls.name: Inner pylons jettison cover (pylons 1-2)
controls.text: This cover protects the button for dropping everything from the inner wing stations.
controls.context: The inner button is the partner of the outer one and is covered in the same way, so it cannot be hit by accident.

controls.name: Inner pylons emergency jettison button
controls.text: This button drops all the weapons and tanks from the inner wing stations (1 and 2) at once.
controls.context: It is for emergencies. The button is under a red cap.

controls.name: Wing fuel tanks drop cover
controls.text: This cover protects the button that drops the two extra fuel tanks under the wings.
controls.context: The pilot lifts it before pressing the button.

controls.name: Wing fuel tanks jettison button
controls.text: This button drops the extra fuel tanks that hang under the wings.
controls.context: Dropping empty tanks makes the plane lighter and faster.

controls.name: Emergency missile / rocket launch cover
controls.text: This cover protects the emergency launch button for missiles and rockets.
controls.context: The pilot lifts the cover first.

controls.name: Emergency missile / rocket launch button
controls.text: This button fires missiles or rockets in an emergency, without going through the normal weapon system.
controls.context: The game names it 'Emergency Missile/Rocket Launch'.

controls.name: Tactical release switch cover
controls.text: This cover protects the tactical release switch.
controls.context: The pilot lifts the cover before moving the switch.

controls.name: Tactical release switch (bombs only)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The bomb fuses are armed; the bombs explode on impact.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The bombs are dropped passive, without exploding.

controls.text: This switch arms the fuses of the bombs, so they explode on impact. With the switch off, the bombs fall but do not explode.
controls.context: The pilot switches it on just before the attack. The manual warns that it must be off when only air-to-air missiles are used.

panels.name: Radar warning receiver SPO-10
panels.text: The SPO-10 is a simple radar warning receiver. It has four small lights, one for each quarter around the plane, and a warning sound. It tells the pilot that an enemy radar is looking at the plane.
panels.context: The lights flash when a radar sweeps the plane. If an enemy radar locks on, all four lights shine steadily and the tone does not stop. The device does not send out any signals.

controls.name: SPO-10 power switch
controls.text: This switch turns the radar warning receiver on or off.
controls.context: The manual says the device is automatic: the pilot only switches it on.

controls.name: SPO-10 test button
controls.text: This button tests the warning receiver by lighting its lights and playing the sound.
controls.context: It is used before flight to see that the device works.

controls.name: SPO-10 volume / mute knob
controls.text: This knob changes the volume of the warning sound, or switches it off.
controls.context: The sound is the main way the pilot is warned, so it should not be turned too low.

controls.name: SPO-10 night / day selector
controls.text: This switch changes the colour of the warning lights. They are white by day and red at night.
controls.context: Red lights do not dazzle the pilot at night.

areas.name: Left console (L segment)
areas.text: The left console holds the throttle and the controls for the engine start, the gear, the flaps, the brakes, the navigation system, the autopilot landing modes and the life support.

panels.name: Engine start and fire extinguisher controls
panels.text: These controls start the engine and put out an engine fire. The MiG-21bis starts quickly: the engine normally runs in 45 seconds.
panels.context: The pilot follows the start-up table: switches on, then the start system, then the start button. If the start does not go as described, the pilot cancels it and starts again.

controls.name: Electric bus No. 1 cover
controls.text: This is the cover over the circuit breaker of the first group of electric lines.
controls.context: The pilot lifts it to reach the breaker.

controls.name: Electric bus No. 1 circuit breaker
controls.text: This is a safety switch for the first group of electric lines of the plane. It cuts the power when too much current flows.
controls.context: The game names it 'Electric Bus Nr.1'. The second bus is on the right wall.

controls.name: Engine start-up system switch
controls.text: This switch turns on the engine start-up system. The game names it 'APU On/Off'.
controls.context: The manual lists it in the start-up table as the step before the engine start button.

controls.name: Engine start-up mode switch (start-up / cold start)

positions.name: COLD START
positions.text: The engine is only spun, without starting.

controls.text: This switch picks the way the engine is started: a real start or a cold start. A cold start only spins the engine without lighting it.
controls.context: The manual says it must be on the start-up position, not on cold start, before the engine start.

controls.name: Engine start-up button
controls.text: This button starts the engine. The pilot presses it for a second or two and the engine begins to turn.
controls.context: After pressing, the pilot waits until the engine is at idle speed. Interrupting the start overloads the electrical system.

controls.name: In-flight engine start-up system switch
controls.text: This switch is for starting the engine again in the air. It supplies 100 percent oxygen to the engine.
controls.context: The game names it 'Engine Emergency Air Start'. It is only used after an engine stop in flight.

controls.name: Fire extinguisher system switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The fire extinguisher system is on.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The fire extinguisher system is off.

controls.text: This switch turns on the fire extinguisher system of the engine compartment.
controls.context: The manual lists it as switched on during the first start-up steps.

controls.name: Fire extinguisher button cover
controls.text: This is the cover over the engine fire extinguisher button.
controls.context: The pilot lifts it before pressing the button.

controls.name: Engine fire extinguisher button
controls.text: Pressing this button discharges the fire extinguisher into the engine compartment.
controls.context: The pilot uses it when a fire warning light shows that the engine is on fire.

panels.name: Engine, nozzle and afterburner controls
panels.text: These switches handle the engine's extra parts: the doors that keep the compressor steady, the cone at the air intake, the nozzle at the rear and the afterburner.
panels.context: The afterburner is extra fuel burned at the back of the engine for much more push. The MiG-21bis has two stages of afterburner.

controls.name: Engine compressor anti-surge doors control switch

positions.name: MANUAL
positions.text: The pilot opens the doors by hand.

controls.text: This switch decides whether the anti-surge doors of the engine work by themselves (automatic) or are opened by hand (manual).
controls.context: The manual says to open them by hand with this switch if the engine surges, which is a rough, shaking airflow in the compressor.

controls.name: Nose cone control switch (automatic / manual)

positions.name: MANUAL
positions.text: The pilot sets the cone with the knob.

controls.text: This switch sets the control of the air intake cone to automatic or to manual.
controls.context: If the automatic system fails, the pilot sets the cone by hand with the knob at the cone gauge, following the manual's table.

controls.name: Emergency nozzle 2-position switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The emergency nozzle control is on.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The emergency nozzle control is off.

controls.text: This switch sets the engine nozzle to one of two fixed positions by hand, maximal or afterburner, if the automatic system fails.
controls.context: The game names it 'Nozzle, Emergency Control'. It is for an emergency only.

controls.name: Afterburner / maximum switch
controls.text: This switch controls the first afterburner and the 100 percent engine speed setting, called maximal.
controls.context: The pilot uses it on the take-off run: with it on, the first afterburner lights after the engine is at full power.

controls.name: Second (emergency) afterburner switch
controls.text: This switch turns on the second afterburner stage, for even more push.
controls.context: The game names it 'Emergency Afterburner'. A light on the warning table shows that it is engaged.

panels.name: Landing gear, flaps and brake controls
panels.text: These controls move the wheels and flaps and handle the brakes and the drag parachute. The gear lever has a safety lock, and the lights beside it show the position of gear, flaps and air brakes.
panels.context: The gear lever has three positions. After the gear is up, it is moved to neutral to save compressed air that brakes the wheels. The brakes and the parachute need that air.

controls.name: Landing gear lever safety lock

positions.name: ENGAGED
positions.text: The gear lever cannot be moved up.

positions.name: RELEASED
positions.text: The gear lever can be moved up.

controls.text: This lock stops the landing gear lever from being moved up on the ground by mistake.
controls.context: The lock is engaged at the start of every mission. The pilot releases it by moving it up before retracting the gear.

controls.name: Landing gear lever (up / neutral / down)

positions.name: NEUTRAL
positions.text: The lever is in the middle; the gear stays where it is.

controls.text: This lever raises or lowers the wheels. The middle position is neutral.
controls.context: The manual says to put the lever in neutral after the gear is up, so no compressed air is wasted braking the wheels.

controls.name: Landing gear lights (warning, up, down)
controls.text: These lights show where the wheels are. Green lights say the gear is down, red lights say it is up, and the warning light says the flaps are out while the gear is up.
controls.context: The warning message reads 'Extract landing gears'. The pilot checks the lights after raising or lowering the gear.

controls.name: Flaps out light
controls.text: This light shows that the flaps are out. Flaps are parts of the wing that give more lift at low speed.
controls.context: The pilot sees it on the panel when the flaps are lowered for take-off or landing.

controls.name: Air brakes out light
controls.text: This light shows that the air brakes are fully out. Air brakes are panels that open into the wind to slow the plane.
controls.context: It is on the same panel as the gear and flaps lights.

controls.name: Flaps retracted button
controls.text: This button pulls the flaps in, up into the wing.
controls.context: The pilot presses it at about 100 metres after take-off and after landing.

controls.name: Flaps take-off position button
controls.text: This button sets the flaps to the take-off position, 25 degrees.
controls.context: The manual says to check the flaps are at take-off before taxiing. They are also used in the first part of the approach.

controls.name: Flaps landing position button
controls.text: This button sets the flaps to the landing position, 45 degrees.
controls.context: The pilot presses it on the final approach, at about 300 metres.

controls.name: Flaps position reset button
controls.text: This button sets all the flap buttons back to their up position.
controls.context: The manual says it only relieves the springs of the buttons when the plane is not in use, with no practical use in the game.

controls.name: Gear ABS brake system switch
controls.text: This switch turns on the anti-skid system (ABS), which stops the wheels from locking up when braking.
controls.context: It works like the ABS of a car.

controls.name: Aircraft lights switch (landing / taxi / retracted)

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The lights are retracted and off.

controls.text: This switch controls the landing and taxi lights, which can fold into the plane.
controls.context: The manual says to retract them after take-off, because they will break above 700 km/h.

controls.name: Drag chute release button
controls.text: Pressing this button opens the drag parachute at the tail, to slow the plane after landing.
controls.context: The manual says to use it after touchdown below 320 km/h. The chute uses compressed air, like the brakes.

controls.name: Drag chute jettison cover
controls.text: This is the cover of the button that drops the drag parachute.
controls.context: The pilot lifts it before pressing the button.

controls.name: Drag chute jettison button
controls.text: Pressing this button drops the drag parachute from the plane.
controls.context: The pilot uses it when taxiing, near the place where chutes are dropped.

panels.name: ARU, boundary layer and hydraulic booster controls
panels.text: These switches handle the ARU, which sets how strongly the tail reacts to the stick. They also handle the boundary layer control and the aileron boosters.
panels.context: The ARU is normally automatic. The pilot only moves to manual mode if it fails, and then slows the plane down.

controls.name: ARU-3VM operating mode selector (auto / manual)

positions.name: MANUAL
positions.text: The pilot sets the ARU with the control switch.

controls.text: This switch decides whether the ARU works by itself (auto) or is set by hand (manual).
controls.context: The manual says it should be in automatic for normal flying.

controls.name: ARU-3VM control switch (high speed / low speed)

positions.name: LOW SPEED
positions.text: The ARU moves toward the low-speed setting, the long arm.

positions.name: NEUTRAL
positions.text: The ARU stays where it is.

positions.name: HIGH SPEED
positions.text: The ARU moves toward the high-speed setting, the short arm.

controls.text: In manual mode, this switch moves the ARU toward the setting for high speed or for low speed.
controls.context: The manual says it only has an effect in manual mode. The pilot watches the ARU gauge while using it.

controls.name: SPS (boundary layer control) switch
controls.text: This switch turns on the boundary layer control system, which blows air over the wing flaps to help the plane at slow landing speeds.
controls.context: The manual says the landing weights for unpaved runways assume the system is used.

controls.name: Ailerons hydro boosters switch
controls.text: This switch turns the hydraulic boosters of the ailerons on or off. The boosters help to move the roll surfaces.
controls.context: The game names it 'Aileron Boosters'.

controls.name: Missile lock sound volume knob
controls.text: This knob sets how loud the tone of a locking heat-seeking missile is.
controls.context: The game names it 'Missile Seeker Sound'. The pilot needs to hear this tone and see the lock light.

panels.name: RSBN / PRMG navigation and landing panel
panels.text: RSBN and PRMG are a short-range navigation and landing system. Beacons near the airfield tell the plane the direction and distance, and guide it to the runway. This panel tunes the system.
panels.context: In the game the stations are made from the runway positions of the airfields. The pilot chooses a station by a channel number and reads the result on the NPP dial and the RSBN distance counter.

controls.name: RSBN / ARC mode selector

positions.name: RSBN
positions.text: The compass needle points to the RSBN station.

positions.name: ARC
positions.text: The compass needle points to the radio compass beacon.

controls.text: This selector picks which station the compass needle of the NPP points to: an RSBN station or a radio compass beacon (ARC).
controls.context: The manual says the distance counter always shows the RSBN station, no matter how this selector is set.

controls.name: RSBN / PRMG operating mode selector
controls.text: This selector picks the working mode of the RSBN receiver: descend (through clouds), navigation or landing.
controls.context: The modes are explained in the manual's navigation chapter.

controls.name: RSBN sound control knob
controls.text: This knob sets the volume of the Morse code of the RSBN station. The code names the station.
controls.context: The pilot listens to the code to make sure which station was picked.

controls.name: RSBN navigation channel selector knob
controls.text: This knob picks the channel of the RSBN navigation station. The game names it 'RSBN Navigation'.
controls.context: The window beside it shows the chosen channel.

controls.name: RSBN navigation channel indicator
controls.text: This window shows the channel set for the navigation station.
controls.context: It is read together with the navigation channel knob.

controls.name: RSBN landing (PRMG) channel selector knob
controls.text: This knob picks the channel of the landing station, PRMG. The game names it 'PRMG Landing'.
controls.context: The window beside it shows the chosen channel.

controls.name: RSBN landing channel indicator
controls.text: This window shows the channel set for the landing station.
controls.context: It is read together with the landing channel knob.

controls.name: RSBN azimuth and distance correction lights
controls.text: These two lights are on when the navigation signal and the landing signal have been received. If the signals are weak or the station is out of range, one or both lights are off.
controls.context: The lights tell the pilot that the system works before it is trusted.

controls.name: RSBN azimuth correction switch
controls.text: The game names this switch 'RSBN Bearing'. The cockpit list calls it the azimuth correction switch.
controls.context: The manual does not describe it further.

controls.name: RSBN distance correction switch
controls.text: The game names this switch 'RSBN Distance'. The cockpit list calls it the distance correction switch.
controls.context: The manual does not describe it further.

controls.name: RSBN reset button
controls.text: The game names this button 'RSBN Reset'. The cockpit list has a zero azimuth set button in this place.
controls.context: The manual does not describe it further.

controls.name: RSBN identify button
controls.text: The game names this button 'RSBN Identify'. It has no description in the manual.
controls.context: It sits on the panel with the other RSBN controls.

controls.name: RSBN test button
controls.text: While this button is held, the compass needle turns to 177 degrees and the distance counter shows 199 km. This tests the RSBN and PRMG receivers.
controls.context: After the button is released, the dials go back to normal.

panels.name: Autopilot (SAU-23ESN) control panel
panels.text: The autopilot, called SAU, is a helper that steadies the plane or flies it back to level. This panel switches its landing modes and its stabilizing mode.
panels.context: The panel is next to two buttons on the stick that start and stop the autopilot recovery mode. The manual says to switch a mode off first if the pilot suspects an error.

controls.name: Autopilot landing mode directional button
controls.text: This lamp button starts the directional landing mode of the autopilot, which flies the plane by the landing system signals. The game names it 'SAU - Landing - Command'.
controls.context: The directional and the automatic landing modes cannot be on together.

controls.name: Autopilot landing mode automatic button
controls.text: This lamp button starts the automatic landing mode of the autopilot.
controls.context: Only one landing mode can be on at a time.

controls.name: Autopilot stabilization button
controls.text: This lamp button turns on stabilization mode. The autopilot then dampens shaking and holds the plane's attitude when the stick is not held.
controls.context: The pilot switches it off with the stick button. The manual says to disengage it after take-off and after landing.

controls.name: Autopilot disengage landing modes button
controls.text: This button switches off the landing mode of the autopilot that is on.
controls.context: The game names it 'SAU Reset/Off'.

controls.name: Autopilot stabilization / recovery light
controls.text: This light is on while the autopilot recovery mode is active.
controls.context: The pilot starts the recovery mode with a button on the stick and ends it with the disengage button.

controls.name: Autopilot low altitude mode switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The low altitude recovery is on.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The low altitude recovery is off.

controls.text: This switch turns on or off the low altitude recovery of the autopilot, which pulls the plane up when it is too low.
controls.context: The manual says the recovery does not work with the gear out and may be rough.

panels.name: Life support, canopy and ejection controls
panels.text: These controls look after the pilot: oxygen and breathing air, the heating and ventilation of the helmet and cockpit, the canopy and the ejection seat.
panels.context: At altitude the air is too thin to breathe, so the pilot gets oxygen through the mask. The switches here set what the pilot breathes and how warm the cockpit is.

controls.name: Mixture / 100% oxygen switch

positions.name: MIX
positions.text: The pilot breathes a mix of air and oxygen.

controls.text: This switch decides what the pilot breathes: a mix of air and oxygen or pure oxygen.
controls.context: The game names it 'Air - Mix / 100% O2'.

controls.name: Emergency oxygen switch
controls.text: This switch turns on the emergency oxygen supply.
controls.context: It is for an oxygen failure. The pilot sees the oxygen pressure on the gauges.

controls.name: Helmet ventilation switch
controls.text: This switch turns the air ventilation of the pilot's helmet on or off.
controls.context: The game names it 'Helmet Air Condition'.

controls.name: Pilot oxygen gauges and breathing indicator
controls.text: These gauges show the oxygen: the level and the breathing indicator, the pressure of the pilot's oxygen and the pressure of the engine's emergency oxygen.
controls.context: The pilot watches them to know how long the oxygen lasts.

controls.name: Helmet glass quick heating button
controls.text: This button heats the glass of the pilot's helmet quickly, so it does not fog up.
controls.context: The game names it 'Helmet Quick Heat'.

controls.name: Helmet glass heating mode switch (auto / manual)
controls.text: This switch sets the heating of the helmet glass to automatic or manual.
controls.context: The game names it 'Helmet Heat'.

controls.name: Cockpit air-conditioning switch (off / cold / auto / warm)
controls.text: This four-position switch sets the cockpit climate: off, cold air, automatic or warm air.
controls.context: The game names it 'Cockpit Air Condition'.

controls.name: Cockpit pressurization lever
controls.text: This lever fills the rubber seal around the canopy with compressed air, so the cockpit is airtight.
controls.context: The manual says it is used after the canopy is locked. The game names it 'Hermetize Canopy'.

controls.name: Canopy lock lever
controls.text: This lever locks the canopy in its closed position.
controls.context: The manual says the pilot locks the canopy with this lever first and then fills the seal with the pressurization lever.

controls.name: Cockpit lock / pressurization warning light
controls.text: This light warns that the canopy is not locked or the cockpit is not pressurized.
controls.context: It is on at the start of the mission and goes off when the canopy is locked.

controls.name: Canopy close button
controls.text: The game names this button 'Canopy Close'. It closes or opens the canopy.
controls.context: The manual does not describe it.

controls.name: Canopy open button
controls.text: The game names this button 'Canopy Open'. It opens the canopy.
controls.context: The manual does not describe it.

controls.name: Canopy anti-icing lever
controls.text: This lever heats the front canopy to keep ice off it. The game names it 'Canopy Anti Ice'.
controls.context: The cockpit list calls it the anti-icing system lever.

controls.name: Helmet visor switch
controls.text: The game names this switch 'Helmet visor - off/on'. It moves the visor of the helmet.
controls.context: The manual does not describe it.

controls.name: Anti-g suit air pressure valve
controls.text: This valve sets the pressure of the anti-g suit. The suit squeezes the pilot's legs in hard turns, so blood stays in the head.
controls.context: The manual says it is not meant for the pilot to use in flight. The game names it 'G-Suit Max/Min valve'.

controls.name: Suit ventilation knob
controls.text: The game names this knob 'Suit Ventilation'.
controls.context: The manual does not describe it. The cockpit list has a hermetic suit pressure control knob and a lever on the left wall.

controls.name: Hermetic suit pressure control knob and lever
controls.text: The cockpit list shows a knob and a lever that set the pressure of the pilot's hermetic suit.
controls.context: The manual lists them in the drawing of the left segment only.

controls.name: Ejection seat up / down set switch
controls.text: This switch moves the pilot's ejection seat up or down.
controls.context: It is listed in the drawing of the left segment. The game has no clickable control for it.

controls.name: Ejection seat emergency oxygen switch
controls.text: The game names this switch 'Ejection Seat Emergency Oxygen'. It belongs to the ejection seat.
controls.context: The manual does not describe it.

controls.name: Ejection handle (Eject)
controls.text: Pulling this handle shoots the pilot out of the plane in the seat. This is the last resort.
controls.context: The game names it 'Eject'. The manual lists the ejection handle in the drawing of the stick segment.

controls.name: UK-2M microphone amplifier GS / KM switch
controls.text: This switch is for the microphone amplifier of the radio. It has two positions named GS and KM.
controls.context: The manual only lists this switch in its drawing and does not explain the two positions.

controls.name: UK-2M microphone amplifier M / L switch
controls.text: This switch is for the microphone amplifier of the radio. It has two positions named M and L.
controls.context: The manual lists it next to the GS / KM switch and does not explain the positions either.

controls.name: UK-2M microphone amplifier preset knob
controls.text: This knob presets the microphone amplifier.
controls.context: The manual says it is not meant for the pilot to use.

areas.name: Right vertical panel (RV)
areas.text: The right vertical panel holds the radio, the radio compass, the transponders, the radar control and the switches that power the navigation devices and the weapons.

panels.name: Radio station panel
panels.text: This panel runs the voice radio for talking to the tower, other aircraft and ground controllers. It has 20 stored channels.
panels.context: The pilot picks a channel before calling the tower. The radio needs 5 to 10 seconds to warm up. With the power switch down, the radio works as an intercom to the ground crew.

controls.name: Radio station power switch

positions.name: DOWN
positions.text: The radio works as an intercom to the ground crew.

controls.text: This switch turns the voice radio on. In the other position the radio only works as the phone line to the ground crew.
controls.context: The ground crew is reached in the down position, for example to talk about repairs or refuelling. For normal flying the switch is up.

controls.name: Radio station volume control knob
controls.text: This knob makes the radio louder or quieter.
controls.context: The pilot sets it so that voices are easy to hear.

controls.name: Radio or compass sound selector switch

positions.name: RADIO
positions.text: Only the radio station is heard.

positions.name: COMPASS
positions.text: The radio station and the radio compass beacon are heard together.

controls.text: This switch picks what the pilot hears: only the radio station, or the radio station and the radio compass beacon together.
controls.context: The pilot needs the compass position to hear the Morse code that names a beacon.

controls.name: Radio noise squelch switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The noise cancelling is on; the radio is quiet when nobody talks.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The noise cancelling is off; weak stations are heard better but the hiss stays.

controls.text: This switch takes the background hiss away when nobody talks, or lets it through so a faint station is heard better.
controls.context: The manual says the pilot can switch the noise cancelling off for a distant station. The station is then clearer but the hiss stays.

controls.name: Radio channel window
controls.text: This small window shows the radio channel that is set. The channels are numbered 0 to 19, where 0 is the 20th.
controls.context: The channels are preset with the radio frequencies of the airfields, which the pilot can see on the kneeboard.

controls.name: Radio channel selector knob
controls.text: This cross-shaped knob picks the radio channel. Turning it to either side steps through the channels.
controls.context: It is used to call the tower or other stations, whose channels are set in the mission.

panels.name: ARC radio compass panel
panels.text: The radio compass (ARC) finds ground radio beacons and shows the direction to them on the compass dial. This panel switches it on and picks the beacon.
panels.context: The pilot picks one of nine stored beacons with a button. The needle on the compass dial turns toward the beacon. It needs 5 to 10 seconds to warm up.

controls.name: ARC power switch
controls.text: This switch turns the radio compass on or off.
controls.context: It is one of the switches turned on after the engine start.

controls.name: ARC operating mode switch (Compass / Antenna)

positions.name: COMPASS
positions.text: The compass finds the beacon and shows its direction.

positions.name: ANTENNA
positions.text: The device works as a plain receiver without direction finding.

controls.text: This switch picks the mode of the radio compass. In compass mode it shows the direction to the beacon. In antenna mode it only listens.
controls.context: The manual says antenna mode is a backup that has no practical use in the game.

controls.name: ARC channel buttons 1-9
controls.text: These nine buttons pick one of nine stored beacon frequencies. The window next to each button shows its number and glows at night.
controls.context: The pilot presses the button of the beacon he wants, for example the airfield's beacon, and the compass needle swings toward it.

controls.name: ARC frequency range selector knob
controls.text: This switch chooses the frequency range of the radio compass. The game lists the positions I-1, I-2, II-1, II-2, III-1, III-2 and more.
controls.context: The game names it 'ARK Zone'. The manual only lists the knob in its drawing.

controls.name: ARC sound control knob (Morse code volume)
controls.text: This knob sets how loud the Morse code of the beacon is. The code is a few letters that name the beacon.
controls.context: The pilot listens to the code to be sure which beacon the compass has found.

controls.name: ARC change button
controls.text: The game names this button 'ARK Change'. The manual describes a button on the radio compass panel that hands control over from the panel in the nose, with no practical use in the game.
controls.context: The manual does not name the button further.

controls.name: Far / near landing beacon switch

positions.name: FAR
positions.text: The far landing beacon is selected.

positions.name: NEAR
positions.text: The near landing beacon is selected.

controls.text: This switch picks the far or the near beacon on the approach to the runway. Landing beacons stand at set distances in front of the runway.
controls.context: The game names it 'Marker Far/Near'. The pilot hears a short beep when flying over a landing beacon.

controls.name: ARC to landing beacon self-adjustment light
controls.text: This light shows that the radio compass has tuned itself to a landing beacon.
controls.context: The manual lists it in the drawing of the central segment.

panels.name: SOD-57 transponder and IFF panels
panels.text: A transponder is a radio box that answers the questions of ground radars with a code, so they can tell friendly aircraft. The MiG-21bis has the SOD-57 for air traffic control and two IFF boxes for identifying friend or foe.
panels.context: The pilot switches the SOD on during start-up and checks that its channel is right. The IFF boxes are for the military side.

controls.name: SOD-57 power switch
controls.text: This switch turns on the SOD-57, the transponder that answers ground radars.
controls.context: The manual lists it among the switches to turn on before taxiing.

controls.name: SOD-57 channel (wave) selector
controls.text: This switch picks the channel the transponder uses. The game labels the positions 3, 1 and 2.
controls.context: The pilot checks that the right channel is set.

controls.name: SOD-57 modes panel
controls.text: The game names this control 'SOD Modes'. It is the mode panel of the transponder.
controls.context: The manual lists it in the drawing of the right segment; it does not describe it further.

controls.name: SOD-57 interrogation button
controls.text: The game names this button 'SOD Identify'. The manual lists it as the transponder's interrogation button.
controls.context: It is not described further in the manual.

controls.name: SOD control block test buttons PBU-1 and PBU-2
controls.text: These two buttons test the control blocks of the transponder. The game names them 'SOD Control PBU-1' and 'PBU-2'.
controls.context: The manual lists them as test buttons in its drawing.

controls.name: SOD-57 identification button (left side)
controls.text: This button on the left wall is the identification button of the SOD-57 transponder.
controls.context: The cockpit list shows it on the left wall, away from the other transponder controls on the right.

controls.name: SOD-57 emission indicator light
controls.text: This light shows that the transponder is sending its answer.
controls.context: It sits on the main panel so the pilot sees it at a glance.

controls.name: Type 81 IFF transponder switch
controls.text: This switch turns on the Type 81 IFF transponder, a radio box that answers who-are-you questions.
controls.context: The game names it 'IFF System Type 81'.

controls.name: SRZO-2 (IFF) coder / decoder power switch
controls.text: This switch turns on the SRZO-2, a second IFF device that sends and reads secret code signals.
controls.context: The manual lists it as the last step of the weapons power-up sequence before taxiing.

controls.name: SRZO codes switch and control lights
controls.text: The game names this switch 'SRZO Codes'. The manual lists three control lights of the SRZO-2, for emitter on, code on and decipher on, together with a channel selector.
controls.context: The manual does not describe the switch further.

controls.name: Emergency transponder cover
controls.text: This cover protects the switch of the emergency transponder.
controls.context: The pilot lifts the cover before moving the emergency transponder switch.

controls.name: Emergency transponder switch
controls.text: The game names this switch 'Emergency Transmitter On/Off'. It is part of the panel with the SRZO-2 self-destruction control.
controls.context: The manual does not describe it further.

controls.name: SRZO self-destruct cover
controls.text: This cover protects the button that destroys the SRZO-2 secret coding device.
controls.context: The pilot lifts the cover before pressing the button.

controls.name: SRZO self-destruct button
controls.text: This button starts the self-destruction of the SRZO-2 IFF device.
controls.context: It is under a cover, and the manual lists it with the emergency transponder panel.

panels.name: Systems power switches (right vertical panel)
panels.text: This block of switches gives electric power to the plane's systems one by one: the nose cone, the spare hydraulic pump, the trimmer, the navigation devices and the autopilot.
panels.context: The pilot turns these on after the engine runs, in the order of the start-up table. Each switch only powers its own device.

controls.name: Nose cone power switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The nose cone has no power.

controls.text: This switch gives power to the movable cone in the air intake. The cone moves in and out to suit the speed of the plane.
controls.context: The manual says to leave it on with the cone control in automatic mode.

controls.name: Auxiliary hydraulic pump switch
controls.text: This switch turns on the spare (emergency) hydraulic pump. Hydraulics move heavy parts with oil under high pressure.
controls.context: The manual lists it in the start-up sequence with the switches for the nose cone and the air bleed doors.

controls.name: Trimmer power switch
controls.text: This switch gives power to the trimmer, which makes small adjustments so the plane flies straight without pushing on the stick.
controls.context: The pilot switches it on in the start-up sequence. The trim button on the stick only works with it on.

controls.name: Radio altimeter / marker power switch
controls.text: This switch turns on the radio altimeter, which measures the height above the ground, and the marker beacon receiver.
controls.context: It is switched on in start-up. When it is on, a short beep is heard over a marker beacon.

controls.name: RSBN / PRMG power switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The navigation and landing system is on.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The navigation and landing system is off.

controls.text: This switch turns on RSBN and PRMG, the short-range navigation and landing system with ground beacons.
controls.context: It needs the KPP and NPP switched on too. The system warms up for 5 to 10 seconds.

controls.name: KPP main / auxiliary power switch

positions.name: MAIN
positions.text: The KPP runs on the main supply.

positions.name: AUXILIARY
positions.text: The KPP runs on the auxiliary supply.

controls.text: This switch picks the main or the auxiliary power for the KPP, the artificial horizon.
controls.context: The manual says the main position is required for normal operation.

controls.name: NPP power switch
controls.text: This switch turns on the NPP, the compass dial that shows heading and the direction to radio stations.
controls.context: The NPP adjusts itself after switching on. Many other systems need its data.

controls.name: Autopilot power switch (SAU)
controls.text: This switch gives power to the autopilot, called SAU. The autopilot is a helper that can keep the plane steady or level it.
controls.context: The pilot can switch the autopilot completely off with this switch if he suspects an error in it.

controls.name: Autopilot pitch channel power switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The pitch channel has no power.

controls.text: This switch gives power to the pitch part of the autopilot, which controls the nose up and down.
controls.context: It is switched together with the main autopilot switch.

controls.name: Main and auxiliary air pressure gauge
controls.text: This gauge shows the pressure of the main and the auxiliary air system.
controls.context: The manual lists it only in the drawing of the right segment.

panels.name: Weapon power switches (right vertical panel)
panels.text: These switches give power to the weapon system. Without them, nothing can be fired even when the sight and the buttons are working.
panels.context: The manual says weapons must never be armed on the ground. The pilot turns them on in steps: pylons, missiles, then the launch switch just before using rockets or missiles.

controls.name: Missiles / rockets heating switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The heating and controller are on.

controls.text: This switch turns on the heating for the infrared and radar missiles and for the gun camera.
controls.context: The manual's start-up table calls it 'Missile Controller Power' and turns it on when infrared or radar missiles are on board.

controls.name: Missiles / rockets launch switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: Rockets and missiles cannot be launched.

controls.text: This switch is the last safety before launching rockets or missiles. With it off, nothing can be launched.
controls.context: The manual says to turn it on just before using rockets or missiles.

controls.name: Pylons 1-2 power switch
controls.text: This switch gives power to the two inner wing stations, so weapons there can be released.
controls.context: The pylons are the pegs under the wings that carry the weapons. The manual says to turn on both pylon switches first.

controls.name: Pylons 3-4 power switch
controls.text: This switch gives power to the two outer wing stations, so weapons there can be released.
controls.context: It is the partner of the pylons 1-2 switch.

controls.name: Gsh-23 gun power switch
controls.text: This switch gives power to the 23 mm cannon.
controls.context: The manual says to turn it on a minute or two before using the gun. The gun also must be loaded with the load buttons.

controls.name: ASP-PFD optical sight power switch
controls.text: This switch turns on the optical gunsight.
controls.context: The sight can be turned on any time the AC power and the gyros are running.

controls.name: Gun camera power switch
controls.text: This switch turns on the gun camera, which films the aiming view.
controls.context: It is one of the weapon-area switches on the right panel.

panels.name: RP-22 radar control panel
