panels.text: This panel controls the plane's radar, called RP-22 Sapphire. The radar finds other aircraft in front of the plane and measures their distance for the weapons.
panels.context: The radar needs 3 to 5 minutes to warm up in standby. It can then run for only about 20 to 25 minutes, so the pilot switches it on only when needed.

controls.name: RP-22 radar main mode switch (Off / Standby / On)

positions.name: STANDBY
positions.text: The radar warms up and waits.

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The radar searches and can lock targets.

controls.text: This switch turns the radar off, lets it warm up in standby, or turns it fully on.
controls.context: The pilot puts it to standby when ready for take-off. The standby time can last 35 to 40 minutes.

controls.name: RP-22 radar error light
controls.text: This red light comes on when the radar has a fault.
controls.context: If it comes on while the radar is in use, the manual says to turn the radar off.

controls.name: RP-22 low altitude / sidebeam compensation switch

positions.name: COMP
positions.text: The radar tries to erase the lower side-lobes.

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The antenna tilts up by about 1.5 degrees.

controls.text: This switch cleans up the radar picture when flying low, where the ground makes clutter at the bottom of the screen.
controls.context: The manual says the middle position erases the lower side-lobes and the top position tilts the antenna up by about 1.5 degrees.

controls.name: RP-22 low altitude light
controls.text: This light shows that the low altitude compensation is active.
controls.context: It sits above the low altitude switch.

controls.name: RP-22 radar fixed beam switch
controls.text: This switch locks the radar beam along the gun and weapon line, to measure the distance to a ground target straight ahead.
controls.context: The pilot uses it for attacking ground targets, so the sight gets an exact distance.

controls.name: RP-22 fixed beam light
controls.text: This light shows that the fixed beam mode is on.
controls.context: It sits above the fixed beam switch.

panels.name: Emergency levers and other right-wall controls
panels.text: These controls are on the right wall: the emergency handle for the landing gear, the handle that throws the canopy off, and a few other items.
panels.context: The two emergency handles are only used when something has failed. They are pulled hard and cannot be undone in flight.

controls.name: Emergency gear extraction lever (main gear)
controls.text: Pulling this lever lowers the main landing gear with the emergency system, if the normal system does not work.
controls.context: The manual says it is used for hydraulic problems when the normal extraction cannot work.

controls.name: Emergency canopy jettison lever
controls.text: Pulling this handle throws the canopy, the glass roof, off the plane.
controls.context: This is for emergencies on the ground or before ejecting.

controls.name: Canopy air conditioner open / close handle
controls.text: This handle opens or closes the ventilation of the canopy.
controls.context: The game names it 'Canopy Ventilation System'.

controls.name: Electric bus No. 2 circuit breaker

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The second bus is cut off.

controls.text: This is a safety switch for the second group of electric lines of the plane. A group of lines that feed equipment is called a bus.
controls.context: A circuit breaker cuts the power when something takes too much. The game names it 'Electric Bus Nr.2'.

controls.name: Fuses / circuit breakers box
controls.text: This is the box with the fuses and circuit breakers on the right wall.
controls.context: The manual lists it in the drawing only; the game has no clickable control for it.

controls.name: Harness separation switch
controls.text: The game names this switch 'Harness Separation'. It belongs to the pilot's seat belts.
controls.context: The manual does not describe it.

controls.name: Harness loose / tight knob
controls.text: The game names this knob 'Harness Loose/Tight'. It makes the pilot's seat belts looser or tighter.
controls.context: The manual does not describe it.

areas.name: Right horizontal panel (RH)
areas.text: The right horizontal panel holds the electric power switches, the fuel pumps and the light controls.

panels.name: Electric power switches (right horizontal panel)
panels.text: These switches make and spread the plane's electricity: the battery, the two generators and the converters that change one kind of electricity into another.
panels.context: The pilot switches them on first when climbing into the cockpit. The manual says to check the battery voltage first, then the converters, then the generator.

controls.name: Battery switch
controls.text: This switch connects the battery to the plane. The battery stores electricity for when the engine is off.
controls.context: The manual says the battery should show at least 24.5 volts before start. The pilot checks it on the voltmeter.

controls.name: Battery heating switch
controls.text: This switch turns on the heating of the battery.
controls.context: The manual says the battery freezes above 4000 metres without heating, so the pilot turns it on before take-off.

controls.name: PO-750 converter No. 1 switch
controls.text: This switch turns on converter No. 1. A converter changes the battery's direct current into the alternating current some instruments need.
controls.context: If this converter fails, the radio, ARC, oil gauge, nose cone and fuel gauge fail together, and the pilot uses the emergency converter.

controls.name: PO-750 converter No. 2 switch
controls.text: This switch turns on converter No. 2, the second device that changes the electricity for instruments.
controls.context: The manual says there is no emergency replacement for it. Without it the EGT, fuel flow, oil pressure and hydraulic gauges read nothing.

controls.name: DC generator switch
controls.text: This switch connects the direct-current generator, which makes electricity while the engine runs.
controls.context: If it fails, the voltage slowly falls and the battery lasts for about 15 minutes.

controls.name: AC generator switch
controls.text: This switch connects the alternating-current generator, which makes electricity for the instruments while the engine runs.
controls.context: A red GENERATOR light goes out once it runs.

controls.name: Emergency converter power switch
controls.text: This switch turns on the emergency converter, the spare for converter No. 1.
controls.context: The pilot uses it when converter 1 fails.

controls.name: Gyros switch (DA-200, NPP, SAU, radar)
controls.text: This switch gives power to the gyros of the DA-200 dial, the compass, the autopilot and the radar. A gyro is a fast spinning wheel that keeps a direction steady.
controls.context: The game names it 'DA-200 Signal, Giro, NPP, RLS, SAU Power'. You hear the gyros spin up when it is turned on.

controls.name: Gyros switch (NPP, SAU, radar, KPP)
controls.text: This switch gives power to the gyros of the compass, the autopilot, the radar and the KPP artificial horizon.
controls.context: The game names it 'Giro, NPP, SAU, RLS Signal, KPP Power'. The manual says the KPP cannot be switched off unless all gyros are switched off.

controls.name: Air bleed doors 1.5 Mach test cover
controls.text: This cover protects the 1.5 Mach test button.
controls.context: The pilot lifts the cover before pressing the test button.

controls.name: Air bleed doors 1.5 Mach test button
controls.text: This is the test button for the air bleed doors at 1.5 Mach, one of the engine air doors that open and close with speed.
controls.context: The manual lists it as a test button. The game names it '1.5 Mach Test Button'.

controls.name: Aileron booster disengage test button
controls.text: This button tests the disengaging of the aileron boosters, the hydraulic helpers that move the ailerons (the roll surfaces).
controls.context: The game names it 'BU-45 Buster System Separation'. The manual only lists it as a test button.

panels.name: Fuel pump switches
panels.text: These switches turn the fuel pumps of the tank groups on. The pumps push fuel from the tanks to the engine.
panels.context: The manual says to switch them on before the engine start. In flight the pilot turns off a group pump when its tank is empty, after the warning light.

controls.name: 1st fuel tank group pump switch
controls.text: This switch turns the pump of the first group of fuel tanks on or off.
controls.context: When the light for the 1st group shows empty, the pilot turns this pump off.

controls.name: 3rd fuel tank group pump switch
controls.text: This switch turns the pump of the third group of fuel tanks on or off.
controls.context: When the light for the 3rd group shows empty, the pilot turns this pump off and lands soon.

controls.name: Dispenser (drain) fuel tank pump switch
controls.text: This switch turns on the pump of the dispenser (drain) fuel tank.
controls.context: A light on the warning table shows low fuel pressure or no fuel in the dispenser tank, and the manual says the engine might stop then.

panels.name: Cockpit and external light controls
panels.text: These knobs and the switch control the lights: white light for the start-up, red lights for night flying and the lights on the outside of the plane.
panels.context: The manual says white light is for the start-up only. After the engine runs and the red lights are on, the white light should be off.

controls.name: Cockpit white-lights control knob
controls.text: This knob sets the brightness of the white light that lights the right panel.
controls.context: The white light is used during start-up. It is not good for night flight, so it is turned off later.

controls.name: Red floodlights control knob
controls.text: This knob sets the red floodlights, which light the cockpit softly for night flying.
controls.context: The game names it 'Main Red Lights'. Red light does not spoil night vision.

controls.name: Panel-text red backlights control
controls.text: This knob sets how bright the printed texts on the panels glow.
controls.context: The game names it 'Cockpit Texts Back-light'.

controls.name: Instruments red backlights control
controls.text: This knob sets how bright the dials of the instruments glow.
controls.context: The game names it 'Instruments Back-light'.

controls.name: Formation lights switch

positions.name: MEDIUM
positions.text: The lights burn with medium brightness.

positions.name: STRONG
positions.text: The lights burn with full brightness.

controls.text: This switch sets the brightness of the position lights that are on the wings and tail, also called formation lights.
controls.context: The centre position is off, up is medium, left is weak and right is strong.

panels.name: Flight recorder and SPRD power
panels.text: These switches turn on the flight data recorder and give power to the starting rockets or to the chaff and flare container that uses the same mounts.
panels.context: The recorder works like a black box and saves the flight data once per second. The rocket switches are only needed when starting rockets or the dispenser are hung under the plane.

controls.name: SARPP-12 flight data recorder power switch
controls.text: This switch turns on the SARPP-12, the black box that records the flight.
controls.context: The manual says it records once per second and can store 120 minutes. The records go to the Saved Games folder when the mission ends.

controls.name: SPRD starter power supply switch
controls.text: This switch gives power to the starting rockets (SPRD), which can be hung under the plane to shorten the take-off.
controls.context: The manual says to turn it on, with the drop switch, to use the rockets or the chaff and flare container.

controls.name: SPRD jettison power supply switch
controls.text: This switch gives power to the drop circuit, which lets the starting rockets be thrown off after take-off.
controls.context: The manual says both rocket switches must be on for the rockets and for the chaff and flare container.

areas.name: Stick and throttle
areas.text: The stick between the pilot's knees and the throttle on the left console carry the buttons the pilot needs during a fight.

panels.name: Pilot stick (PS)
panels.text: This is the control stick between the pilot's knees. Moving it forward and back and left and right flies the plane. Buttons on the grip handle the weapons and the autopilot.
panels.context: The ARU sets how strongly the stick moves the tail. The grip carries the gun trigger, the trimmer, the autopilot buttons, the radar lock button and the weapon release.

controls.name: Control stick
controls.text: Moving the stick forward and back lifts or lowers the nose. Moving it left and right rolls the plane.
controls.context: The ARU system changes how much the tail moves for each bit of stick travel, depending on speed and height.

controls.name: Gun trigger
controls.text: Pulling this trigger fires the 23 mm cannon for as long as it is held.
controls.context: The gun will not fire if it is not loaded, the gun switch is off or the landing gear is out.

controls.name: Gun trigger safety

positions.name: SAFE
positions.text: The trigger cannot fire the gun.

positions.name: ARMED
positions.text: The trigger can fire the gun.

controls.text: This safety catch locks the gun trigger. Up is safe and down is armed.
controls.context: The manual describes the trigger as up for SAFE and down for ARMED.

controls.name: Trimmer button (pitch only)
controls.text: This two-way button makes small corrections to the nose up and down position, so the plane flies straight without pressing on the stick.
controls.context: It only changes the pitch. The trimmer power switch on the right panel must be on.

controls.name: Autopilot recovery button
controls.text: This button starts the autopilot recovery mode, which tries to bring the plane back to level flight from any position.
controls.context: The manual says recovery is not always possible. The autopilot power switches must be on.

controls.name: Autopilot disengage button
controls.text: This button ends the autopilot recovery and stabilization modes.
controls.context: The pilot also uses it first if he thinks the autopilot works wrongly.

controls.name: Radar lock-on button
controls.text: Holding this button for 2 to 3 seconds locks the radar on the target under the gate. With the optical sight it also steadies the aiming ring.
controls.context: The pilot holds it until the radar screen changes and the lock light on the sight comes on.

controls.name: Weapon release cover
controls.text: This is the red cap over the weapon release button.
controls.context: The pilot lifts it before using the button.

controls.name: Bomb, rocket and missile release button
controls.text: This button releases bombs, rockets and missiles. It sits under a visible red cap.
controls.context: For missiles and bombs the pilot holds it for about 2 seconds. For rockets, he holds it until the burst ends.

controls.name: Gear brake lever
controls.text: This lever on the back of the grip brakes the wheels. The harder it is pulled, the stronger the brake.
controls.context: The pedals give braking on one side. The manual says to avoid brakes on the take-off run and steer with the rudder.

controls.name: Fuselage (centre) fuel tank jettison button
controls.text: This button drops the extra fuel tank under the belly.
controls.context: The game names it 'Drop Center Fuel Tank'.

panels.name: Throttle (left console)
panels.text: The throttle lever on the left console sets the engine's power. The twist grip, the switches and the buttons on it handle the radar, the sight, the radio and the air brakes.
panels.context: The pilot can keep his hand on the throttle for most things. It has an idle stop and a stop position that need levers to pass.

controls.name: Throttle lever
controls.text: Moving this lever forward gives the engine more power and moving it back gives less. The positions are stop, idle, maximum, afterburner and second afterburner.
controls.context: The manual says the pilot sets idle for the engine start and goes to the afterburner for a take-off.

controls.name: Throttle movement locking lever
controls.text: This lever locks the throttle in place, or frees it again.
controls.context: The game names it 'Throttle Fixation'.

controls.name: Throttle engine-stop and locking lever
controls.text: This lever has to be unlocked before the throttle can move into the engine stop position. The game calls it 'Engine Stop/Lock'.
controls.context: It stops the engine from being shut down by mistake.

controls.name: Throttle rotating cylinder (radar gate / sight ring size)
controls.text: Twisting the grip moves the radar gate up and down on the screen. With the optical sight, it changes the size of the aiming ring to measure the distance.
controls.context: The pilot moves the gate over a target and then presses the lock button on the stick. The game names it 'TDC Range / Pipper Span control'.

controls.name: Airbrake control switch
controls.text: This switch on the throttle grip opens the air brakes into the wind to slow the plane, or closes them again.
controls.context: The pilot uses it to slow down quickly, for example in a dive or on the way to landing.

controls.name: Radio PTT button
controls.text: Holding this button on the throttle lets the pilot speak on the radio.
controls.context: The game names it 'Radio PTT' and offers the intercom menu with it.

controls.name: SPRD drop button (ASO chaff / flares)
controls.text: Pressing this button drops the take-off rockets after take-off. With the chaff and flare container, holding it launches two flares and one chaff every 0.3 seconds.
controls.context: The container holds 64 charges, so the decoys last about 9 seconds. The cockpit does not show how many are left.

controls.name: SPRD drop button cover
controls.text: This is the red cover over the SPRD drop button on the throttle.
controls.context: The pilot lifts it before pressing the button.

areas.name: Help buttons at the back of the cockpit
areas.text: At the back of the cockpit the game has buttons for moving the stick, rudder and throttle, and for the force feedback.

panels.name: Helper buttons for stick and throttle (rear)
panels.text: At the back of the cockpit the game has buttons to move the stick, the rudder and the throttle with the mouse. They are help buttons from the game, not real cockpit parts.
panels.context: The game names them Stick Up, Stick Down, Stick Left, Stick Right, Rudder Left, Rudder Right, Throttle Decrease and Throttle Increase.

controls.name: Stick and rudder helper buttons
controls.text: These six buttons move the stick up, down, left and right, and the rudder left and right, when clicked.
controls.context: The game offers them for use with the mouse. The manual does not describe them.

controls.name: Throttle decrease / increase buttons
controls.text: These two buttons lower or raise the throttle step by step when clicked.
controls.context: The game offers them for use with the mouse, like the stick buttons. The manual does not describe them.

controls.name: Force feedback On / Off button
controls.text: This button switches the force feedback effect of the joystick on or off. Force feedback makes the stick push back like a real one.
controls.context: The game names it 'Force Feedback On/Off'.
